CaptureDetails.description: The Firefox extension sends the pages of the sites you open here — so the application learns about works without requesting anything from the site itself, and sees them as you see them (with your login).
CaptureDetails.firefoxStep1: Open about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox in Firefox — it has to be pasted into the address bar by hand; Firefox won't open it from a link.
CaptureDetails.firefoxStep2: Click “Load Temporary Add-on…” and choose the extension's file — paste its path into the file name field:
CaptureDetails.firefoxStep3: Done: the extension works until Firefox restarts; after a restart it has to be loaded again the same way. After the application is updated, click “Reload” on the extension on the same page.
CaptureDetails.noSources: No source is watching pages in the browser right now.
CaptureDetails.recentNone: None yet. Open a work's page on one of the sites above — it will show up here in a couple of seconds.
CaptureDetails.sent: Only the pages of these sites — and only to the address it is set to: by default {{address}}, this application on this computer. The address is changed in the extension's settings (about:addons → recommend4me → Options; Preferences on macOS and Linux). Pages of other sites go nowhere.
CaptureDetails.shown: On a work's page — a panel with the prediction, the grading buttons and what the prediction rests on. Next to each of the site's tags — the model's confidence in brackets (yellow if more likely not) and your ✓ “yes” and ✕ “no”; pressing again withdraws the answer. After them — your tags, suggestions with a dashed outline and a field to add your own. On ficbook, under the “Пэйринг и персонажи” (pairing and characters) block — the computed pairings and main characters. Under reviews and pictures — “+ / −”: a reason to pick the work or to drop it. In feeds and search, on every card — the prediction and your grade. This can be turned off in the extension's settings.

SafariSteps.heading: Safari on iPad
SafariSteps.intro: Safari won't take an extension that isn't from the App Store, so on the iPad a script for the free Userscripts app does the same: it sends the pages and shows the prediction, the grade and the tags on them.
SafariSteps.notSecure: This window isn't open over https: a script taken from here will call {{origin}}, which the iPad most likely can't reach. Open the application on the iPad at the address from step 1.
SafariSteps.step1: On this computer, serve the application over https through Tailscale once: in the Tailscale network settings (DNS) turn on “HTTPS Certificates”, then run tailscale serve --bg 8095. The application will open at an address like https://computer-name.your-network.ts.net — with no port.
SafariSteps.step2: On the iPad install <link>Userscripts</link> from the App Store, open it once and choose a folder for scripts. Then in “Settings → Apps → Safari → Extensions → Userscripts” turn it on and allow it on all websites.
SafariSteps.step3: In Safari on the iPad open this window at the https address from step 1 and tap the script link below, then the Userscripts icon in the address bar → “Install”. The script remembers the address it was taken from and will update from there.
